text:
toni: heads-up — i pushed a tiny prototype for telemetry egress routing to staging. main thing: we can route spans/metrics/logs by tenant to different exporters/retention. need consensus on retention semantics + SDK init pattern for python/go/rust.

sam: can you TL;DR the routing options? short bullets please.

toni: sure — current prototype supports 3 targets: local-collector (team-managed), long-term-obsv (GCP/AM), and cold-blob (S3). routing policy is pattern-based on tenant id + route tags. examples:

```
otel.egress:
  default: local-collector
  tenant_overrides:
    enterprise-*: long-term-obsv
    debug-* : cold-blob
```

Retention is attached to target: local-collector=7d, long-term-obsv=365d, cold-blob=indefinite(archives).

elaine: i like the idea but worried about SDK behaviour under high QPS. if python app directly exports to long-term-obsv we hit connection churn and quota limits. sidecar/collector solves fanout and backpressure.

kevin: +1 for agent/collector + per-tenant routing in the collector. keeps SDK init tiny and language-agnostic. also lets us centralize batching and retry policies.

sam: what about hybrid — SDKs export to local agent by default, but we optionally allow direct export for very latency-sensitive routes? how would that look in config?

toni: exactly. SDK env defaults to local agent but we support an override env var per route. pseudocode:

```
# python / go / rust envs
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317
REDWOOD_OTEL_EGRESS_POLICY=tenant-routing
REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT=enterprise-*,low-latency-route
```

If REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT matches tenant/route, SDK will attempt direct OTLP->long-term-obsv. Otherwise it exports to local collector.

elaine: how do we express sampling/retention? we should avoid duplicating sampling in SDKs. prefer server-side dynamic sampling (collector) that marks spans with sampling decision for later ingestion.

kevin: agree. collector can implement per-tenant sampling rules and header propagation so downstream storage knows TTL. proposal: add span attribute `redwood.egress_ttl_days` when routing to long-term vs short-term.

sam: any security/compliance concerns if we route tenant traces to cold-blob for e-discovery? need ACLs + audit.

toni: yes — cold-blob writes go to a sealed bucket with KMS + object-level labels. we also emit an audit span/event. will add a retention policy checklist in the PR.

kevin: language integration notes — python: we already ship an init wrapper (redwood_otel.init()). should we add a small egress config to it? go/rust prefer env-driven bootstraps.

elaine: propose minimal SDK changes: 1) default to local collector endpoint 2) honor REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT 3) include tenant-id in resource attributes 4) expose an opt-in `egress_hint` span attribute for route preference.

sam: can you paste example bootstrap for each language so infra can test?

toni: pasted quick examples: 

Python (fastapi):
```
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317
export REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT=
python -m uvicorn app:app
```

Go (net/http):
```bash
export OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317
export REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT=enterprise-*
./app
```

Rust (actix):
```
OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4317 \ 
REDWOOD_OTEL_DIRECT_EXPORT= \ 
./target/release/app
```

kevin: minor: we should document fallback semantics when direct export fails (SDK should fallback to agent instead of dropping spans). also quota-exceeded should switch to local collector on the fly.

toni: noted — fallback policy = immediate fallback to agent + emit a metric. will add to design doc.

infra-bot: deploy-bot: collector-routers v0.3 deployed to staging (config id: r-2026-03-19).

elaine: sweet. i'll spin up a python service with simulated enterprise tenant and hammer it to validate connections + fallback logic.

sam: one more: retention summary must be surfaced in console per-tenant. ops wants a dashboard showing routing breakdown and retention buckets counts.

toni: yep — console workitem created (RFC link in #product). will propose a per-tenant retention column in traces table and a retention_usage graph.

kevin: outgoing action items: 
- toni: update PR with fallback + ttl attribute logic
- elaine: perf run on python SDK with direct export vs agent
- sam: sketch console retention UI
- infra-bot: promote collector config to canary after perf thumbs-up

els: :thumbsup:

sam: thanks. short and actionable. we can iterate on sampling rules later.
